claim: Both move the temple inward: 1823 makes the body a shrine and the heart the great temple, 919 makes the five syllables and the subtle within the temple where the Lord sits.

880 says the mind joined with the breath binds the five senses (ஐம்புலன் கட்டுண்ணும்) and that is release (வீடு). Naladiyar 59 says one who can guard, without wavering, the craving that enters through the five gates of body, mouth, eyes, nose and ears will surely reach release (வீடு பெறும்). Both make holding the five senses the way to வீடு; 880 does it by breath and inner sound, the Naladiyar by firm guarding.

126 makes the thirty-six (tattvas) the rungs of a ladder to release (முப்பதும் ஆறும் படிமுத்தி ஏணியாய்). 2020 says Nandi made known the nature of the thirty-six and then stood beyond them (ஆறாறுக்கு அப்புறம் ஆகி நின்றானே). The ladder of 126 needs the guru's teaching of 2020 to be climbed, and its top is beyond the ladder.

1709 says the fifty letters are set in the adharas and above them, where it wells up, stands the one letter (ஓரெழுத்து). 965 says the fifty letters are all the Vedas and Agamas, and that once one knows what they become they go and become the five letters (அஞ்செழுத்து). Both reduce the fifty letters to fewer; 965 to the five syllables, 1709 further to one letter above them in the body.

867 says the heart resounds with the drum's sound (பறையோசை) in the nine and the sun is the conch (சங்கு) at dawn, with the Supreme standing as a lamp. 606 lists the ten inner sounds, among them conch and drum (வளை பேரி), and says only those who have bowed can perceive them. 606 places 867's drum and conch in the full list of inner nadas and adds the condition for hearing them.

The praise tells Daksha's sacrifice through the punished gods: the moon's body worn, the sun's teeth knocked out, Agni's hand cut off, Brahma's head fallen, Saraswati's nose slipping (சோமன் மேனியுந் தேய ... விதிதலை வீழ நன்பாரதியு மூக்கு நழுவிட). Tirumular's verse lists the same losses, head, face, nose, hand and shoulder, of Hari, Brahma, Daksha, the sun, the moon and Agni (சிரமுக நாசி சிறந்தகை தோள்தான்), as the fate of the good without Hara's grace. The song keeps the list as story, and Tirumular draws the lesson.

1250 names the great maya that looks on the leather bag of the five elements as 'I' (தோற்பை யானாக நோக்கும் மா மாயை) and tends a body that ghosts, vultures, jackals and crows will tear (காக்கை பீறா). Tirumanthiram 167 asks what it matters if crows carry off the nest once the dancer who stood in the skin bag (தோற்பையுள் நின்று ... கூத்தன்) has left it. The Tirumanthiram separates the dweller from the bag; the song names the failure to make that separation as the delusion it cannot end.

b: போதிலி ருந்துவி டாச்சதுர் வேதமொ ழிந்தவ னாற்புளி
போதுயர் செந்தழ லாப்பெரு வானநி றைந்த விடாப்புக
ஆதர வின்பருள் மாக்குரு நாதனெ னும்படி போற்றிட
ஆசையெ ணும்படி மேற்கவி பாடுமி தம்பல பார்த்தடி
காதட ரும்படி போய்ப்பல பூசலி டுங்கய லாற்கனி
காரட ருங்குழ லாற்கிரி யானத னங்களி னாற்கலை
சாதன மென்றுரை யாப்பரி தாபமெ னும்படி வாய்த்திடு
சாகர மன்றெரி யாக்கொடு சூரரு கும்படி யாத்திணி
claim: 373 sets the two gods' failure against the speaker's claim: நானே அறிந்தேன் அவனாண்மையாலே, I knew him by his might. Arunagiri names the same Siva whom Brahma and Vishnu could not find (அரிதான), the fire filling the sky, and asks whether a day will come when he too (அடியேனும்) will know and praise. Tirumular states the knowing as done and as the Lord's gift; Arunagiri keeps it as a hope.

1293 asks for the experience of the feet (அநுபூதி) and describes it as nectar, sugar and honey (ஆரமுதமான சர்க்கரை தேனே). Tirumanthiram 2940 places the light beyond the turiyas within an experience that speech does not reach (உரையில் அநுபூதி). The same word is given tastes in the song and is put beyond words in the Tirumanthiram, so the song's sweetness is a figure for something it cannot state.

After its lovemaking scene, 924 says the Lord's lotus feet with anklets and his golden shoulders with vetchi flowers dance in the poet's eyes (என் நயனத்தில் உற்று நடமிடும்). Kural 1126 has the woman say her lover does not leave her eyes (கண்ணுள்ளின் போகார்) and is not hurt when she blinks. The beloved living in the eyes is given in 924 to the god, in place of the women the song describes.

The Kural says neither shaving nor matted hair is needed if one gives up what the world condemns; 497 asks to be spared ochre, matted hair, forest wandering and fasting and to be given instead the inner knowledge in which the self subsides. Both set the ascetic's outward marks aside, the Kural for conduct, 497 for grace and knowledge.

Both see the body as a bag full of holes (Naladiyar தொளைபலவாய், 534 தொள்ளைப் புலாற்பை). The Naladiyar tells the lover to look at the desired body as a bag turned inside out; 534 turns the image on the poet's own body and asks to be rid of it.
1773 says the Lord is too vast to be walked round; 1774 answers that water, flowers and his name, with knowing, are the way to circle him.

The Kural warns that the sweet words (இன்சொல்) of women who desire wealth rather than love bring harm. The song shows the order exactly: on the bed they say 'first give the gold coins' (பொற்பணம் முதல் நீ தா), and once paid they speak as sweet as milk and honey (ஈந்தால் ... ஆன்பால் தேன் போல செப்பிடும்); the sweet speech is the receipt for the gold.

Both end with Murugan bowing to Valli: in 65 he sees her feet, cries 'refuge' and stands behind her and bows (தஞ்சம் எனும்படி ... கும்பிடும் இளையோனே); in 71 he joins his red hands and bows to her in the millet field (செங்கரம் குவித்துக் கும்பிடும்). In 65 the image mirrors the plea, where the poet asks to cry தஞ்சம் at the Lord's feet.
1003 to 1006 prescribe flowers, pastes and lamps and promise every fruit; 1008 says the Lord's servants, the Siva-yogis and the desireless do not want such ritual work, only love.
